claim: An NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 AI rack draws a total of 132 kW.
team_figure: about 130 kW per AI training rack
note: Same datasheet gives operating power 125kW to 135kW.

claim: The average typical (modal) rack density across Uptime's 2025 survey is almost 9 kW, or 7.5 kW excluding high-density sites.
quote: The average of the modal densities in our total sample reaches almost 9 kW
team_figure: about 10 kW per standard cloud rack
note: Survey covers all operators, not cloud only. Excluding sites at 30 kW or more the figure is 7.5 kW ('comes to 7.5 kW in our 2025 survey').

claim: On-site backup generation of at least 50% of critical load.
note: No public source found for a 50% figure. Data centre electrical designs I opened (CSE magazine, csemag.com/data-center-design-considerations) describe blocks 'supported 100% by its associated electrical system', which is about redundancy topology, not a generation share, so it is not used as the value.

claim: Under the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016, a Part A(1) combustion permit applies to appliances of 50 MW rated thermal input or more, aggregated on one site.
quote: Part A(1) (a) Burning any fuel in an appliance with a rated thermal input of 50 or more megawatts.
note: Aggregation rule: two or more appliances on the same site by the same operator with aggregate 50 MW or more are treated as one.

claim: Medium combustion plant of 1 MW up to 50 MW thermal input also needs an environmental permit under Schedule 25A.
quote: “medium combustion plant” means a combustion plant with a rated thermal input equal to or greater than 1 megawatt but less than 50 megawatts
note: Permitting starts at 1 MW thermal (medium combustion plant and specified generator rules), not 50 MW. 50 MW is the Part A(1) threshold.

claim: A 1:1 ratio of acres to critical MW is given as a general guide for data centre site sizing.
quote: An acre/critical MW ratio of 1:1 is a good general guide
team_figure: about 4 MW of IT load per acre
note: Rule of thumb in an opinion piece, not a standard. The team figure is 4 times this.

claim: The Didcot powered land sale works out at about £677,000 per grid MW.
quote: about £677,000 per grid MW at Didcot
note: Secondary source: Ampervia's own division of £203m for a 300 MW grid connection; the RWE annual report itself was not opened. Per grid MW, not IT MW.

claim: MHCLG/VOA policy-appraisal estimate for a typical industrial site in Nottingham, the nearest listed built-up area to the site, at 1 Oct 2023.
quote: Industrial sheet: East Midlands | E63001992 | Nottingham | 850000 (column £/ha)
team_figure: industrial land value per acre in the East Midlands (no team number given)
note: Published per hectare; 850,000 / 2.471 = about £344,000 per acre by arithmetic. Other East Midlands areas range 500,000 (Lincoln) to 1,000,000 (Northampton). Policy-appraisal values, which the publisher says are not market values. Distribution land for East Midlands is 2,000,000 £/ha on the Distribution sheet.

claim: Caterpillar D250 GC to D600 GC diesel generator sets in a Level 2 sound attenuated enclosure: 71 to 74 dB(A) sound pressure at 7 m.
quote: Sound Pressure Levels (dBA) at 7m (23 ft) ... Level 2 Sound Attenuated Enclosure (Steel) 250 ekW ... 74; 350 ... 71
team_figure: typical generator noise at a stated distance (no team number given)
note: Range is 71 to 74 dB(A) across 250 to 600 ekW. Data centre sets of 2 MW or more will differ.

claim: The UK standard for assessing industrial and commercial sound at homes is BS 4142:2014+A1:2019; the environment agencies' MID supplements it.
quote: This MID supplements BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 Method for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound (BS 4142).
team_figure: UK standard used to assess industrial noise at homes
note: Value is the standard's name, so value is null.
